observations: Under the explicitly assumed atomic single-winner primitive P keyed by stable effect_identity=E, the divergent-payload race still yields exactly one canonical winner and one loser.

Because the loser's intended payload hash differs from the authoritative canonical hash, treating the loser as an idempotent duplicate would be incorrect. The safe local rule is to preserve a payload conflict and issue no second mutation.

The divergent-payload branch therefore requires a stronger reconciliation predicate than effect-identity equality alone: duplicate suppression is permitted only when canonical payload identity matches the intended effect payload; mismatch remains unresolved/conflicting.
inference: Within this exact deterministic model, stable effect identity plus atomic single-winner admission prevents duplicate canonical effects, while payload-hash comparison at authoritative loser reconciliation prevents a divergent intent from being silently collapsed into an idempotent duplicate. This is conditional architecture evidence only: the fixture does not establish that an allowed Chat/repository transport exposes primitive P, authoritative conflict semantics, or linearizable/read-after-write-consistent lookup.
